author: reek
body: The demonstration that `substring` no longer reads past the end of its source. It must DIE on a UD2; if it prints a line, the bounds check is gone.

author: reek
body: The second text is not decoration. Bytes past a string are usually blank, and blank padding and a leaked neighbour look identical -- so the probe puts something recognisable there and the leak becomes unambiguous.

author: reek
body: This carries a `.fatal`, which is worth being honest about: `-Fatal` is not part of any routine battery, and a `.fatal` test has no `.expected` because the captured output is an `!EXC` dump whose RIP moves with every codegen change. So this file is a compile check plus a manual read. The half that a battery can fail on is `codex/test/ops/substring-bounds.codex`, which pins every legal request.
